# Catalog

<!-- Generated by scripts/catalog.js from scripts/categories.json. Do not edit by hand; run `npm run catalog`. -->

**367 skills** (66 slash-command workflows, 301 knowledge skills) · **16 index skills** · **53 subagents** · **30 rules**

Model-visible footprint: ~4696 tokens of Antigravity's 20,000-token customization budget.

## Workflows (slash commands)

| Command | What it does |
| :--- | :--- |
| `/a11y-audit` | Audits a web UI against WCAG 2.2 AA in two passes, automated (axe-core, Lighthouse) and manual (keyboard, focus, screen reader, zoom and reflow, contrast, target size, motion), files ranked findings mapped to success criteria, fixes them at the component level and adds regression tests. |
| `/advisor-council` | Puts a high-stakes decision before a council of independent advisors, each with a distinct lens such as skeptic, operator, user advocate, contrarian or domain expert. |
| `/api-scaffold` | Scaffolds a new API endpoint or service contract-first: learns the project's layering from an existing endpoint, writes the OpenAPI, protobuf or GraphQL contract, adds boundary validation, RFC 9457 errors, auth and per-object authorization, writes failing tests first, implements, and updates docs. |
| `/architecture-decision` | Records an architecture decision as an ADR: frames one decision and its forces, gathers at least two real options with evidence from the code and docs, compares them against weighted drivers, states the decision, consequences and a revisit trigger, and files it in the project's ADR log with status and superseding links. |
| `/blueprint` | Produces a reviewable implementation plan before any code is written: scope, constraints, affected modules found by search, contracts first, risks, and atomic steps that each carry a test. |
| `/bug-variant-hunt` | Takes one confirmed bug or vulnerability, abstracts it into a source, sink and missing-guard pattern, sweeps the codebase for siblings with grep, Semgrep or CodeQL, then proves or refutes every hit with evidence and ranks confirmed variants by reachability and impact. |
| `/build-fix` | Restores a red build, type-check or lint run with the smallest correct changes: captures the output, groups errors by root cause, fixes the earliest first and re-runs after each fix, without suppressing diagnostics. |
| `/checkpoint` | Marks a logical milestone in a long task: runs a quick verification, writes a compact progress summary (done, in progress, next, decisions, gotchas), saves it to the EAG session store, optionally commits with the user's consent, and recommends a fresh conversation to reclaim context. |
| `/ci-failure-triage` | Diagnoses failing CI checks on a pull request or branch: pulls the failed job logs, finds the first real error instead of the cascade after it, classifies the cause (code, test, flaky, environment, cache, dependency drift, permissions or secrets, infrastructure), reproduces it locally and proposes the smallest fix, never disabling checks to go green. |
| `/code-review` | Reviews a diff, branch, pull request or set of files for correctness, security, performance and maintainability defects, and returns ranked findings with exact patches. |
| `/codebase-onboard` | Maps an unfamiliar repository fast: entry points, build and test commands, architecture layers, data flow, key modules and conventions, delegating breadth scans to the codebase-explorer subagent and writing the result as a CODEMAP.md. |
| `/context-driven-tracks` | Runs spec-driven development in tracks. |
| `/cross-model-review` | Gets an independent second opinion on a diff, plan or decision from a different model or a fresh subagent with no shared context: builds a compact self-contained brief, strips secrets, asks consent before anything is sent, then reconciles both reviews into agreed, disputed and single-source findings, each checked against evidence. |
| `/deep-work` | Runs a high-rigor mode for hard problems: restates the problem with testable acceptance criteria, enumerates competing hypotheses, plans with a verification per step, delegates bounded research to subagents, keeps context lean, and holds strict quality gates before claiming done. |
| `/dependency-upgrades` | Upgrades dependencies safely: audits outdated and vulnerable packages, batches them by risk (security fixes, patch and minor, then each major alone), reads changelogs and migration guides, applies codemods, verifies every batch with the project's gates, and sets up Renovate or Dependabot grouping. |
| `/design-interrogation` | Stress-tests a plan, spec or design with a one-question-at-a-time interview that settles upstream decisions before downstream ones, offers a recommended answer with every question, reads the code instead of asking when the code can answer, and ends with a decision log plus optional ADR and glossary entries. |
| `/doc-co-writing` | Co-writes a substantial document with the user, such as a design doc, proposal, RFC, strategy memo or long README: gathers context with targeted questions, agrees an outline, drafts section by section from options the user picks, then has a fresh subagent with no context read it as the target reader and fixes the gaps it finds. |
| `/dockerize` | Containerizes an application end to end: records its runtime contract, writes a multi-stage Dockerfile with a pinned slim or distroless base, non-root user and cache-friendly layers, adds .dockerignore, a healthcheck and a Compose file for local dependencies, then builds, scans, runs and smoke-tests the container. |
| `/docs-to-skill` | Turns a documentation site, a repository's docs folder or a PDF manual into a new skill in the Everything Antigravity format: reads a bounded set of pages, extracts the API surface, core concepts and pitfalls in its own words, distils a 6-12 KB SKILL.md with reference files and cited sources, then tests it with realistic prompts and the validator. |
| `/e2e` | Builds and maintains Playwright end-to-end tests for critical user journeys with page objects, role-based locators, isolated test data and trace-on-retry flake handling, and runs them headed, headless or in CI with artifacts. |
| `/explain-code` | Explains unfamiliar code at the requested depth: a short summary, an annotated walkthrough of the execution path, call graph and data flow, state and side effects, history from git, and the gotchas that bite newcomers, with diagrams in a walkthrough artifact and every claim tied to file:line. |
| `/feature-dev` | Takes a feature from request to a review-ready branch through gated stages: /blueprint, /tdd, implementation, /verify, /code-review and /pr-ready, and delegates planning, test writing and review to subagents when the scope warrants it. |
| `/focus-friendly-output` | Switches the session into an attention-friendly reply style: the single next action comes first, then short numbered chunks, explicit checkpoints that show progress, a quick recap after breaks and a parked list for tangents, with full detail moved lower instead of deleted. |
| `/framework-migration` | Migrates a framework, runtime or major library version in stages: baseline, blast-radius inventory, the official migration guide, a staged plan with green checkpoints, official codemods first, compatibility shims, deprecation burn-down and verification against the baseline. |
| `/fresh-context-loop` | Runs an autonomous build loop in which every iteration starts from a fresh context: it reads a backlog file and a progress log, implements the highest-priority unfinished story, runs typecheck and tests, commits on green and records what it learned, until every story passes or a hard iteration cap is hit. |
| `/game-build` | Scaffolds a playable game prototype fast: picks the engine (Canvas, Phaser, Three.js or Godot) from constraints, builds the core loop on a fixed timestep, ships one mechanic with win and lose states, adds a juice pass (screen shake, hit-stop, particles, SFX) and verifies it runs at 60 fps with no console errors, using the browser for web games. |
| `/git-worktrees` | Runs each task or parallel agent in its own git worktree: picks a worktree root and confirms it is ignored, creates a branch-backed worktree, installs dependencies and proves a green test baseline before any edit, then finishes by merging, opening a PR, keeping or discarding (with confirmation) and cleans up merged branches on evidence. |
| `/harness-audit` | Audits the user's Antigravity setup and scores it: installed plugins, colliding skill, agent and MCP names, always-on rules versus the 20k-token budget, EAG hook health, MCP server and tool bloat, v1 EAG leftovers, and missing project rules. |
| `/human-step-wizard` | Builds a resumable, interactive walkthrough script for setup steps only a person can do: vendor console clicks, creating API keys or OAuth clients, adding CI secrets, DNS changes at a registrar, billing approvals and cutovers. |
| `/idea-to-design` | Turns a rough idea into an approved technical design through dialogue: reads the project first, asks clarifying questions one at a time with multiple choice where possible, proposes two or three materially different approaches with trade-offs and a pick, walks the design section by section for approval, trims it with YAGNI and writes a dated design doc. |
| `/instinct-capture` | Distills a correction, a solved non-obvious bug, or a confirmed preference into an instinct (trigger "when X", action "do Y", evidence, scope, starting confidence), deduplicates it against existing instincts, and records it with the EAG CLI so future sessions start with it. |
| `/instincts` | Reviews and evolves learned EAG instincts: lists them by confidence, reinforces or weakens each based on real outcomes, prunes those below 0.3 after confirmation, promotes proven ones (confidence 0.85 or more, seen 3 or more times) into a project skill, and exports or imports them across machines. |
| `/issue-triage` | Triages bug reports and issues: collects the backlog, reproduces each report, classifies type and area, finds duplicates, assigns a justified priority, and rewrites confirmed bugs as actionable tickets with steps, evidence and acceptance criteria. |
| `/marketing-launch` | Runs a multi-channel launch for a product, major release or open-source project: positioning check, asset list (landing copy, OG image, demo GIF or video, per-channel announcement posts, docs), T-minus timeline, launch-day runbook and post-launch metrics review. |
| `/merge-conflict-resolution` | Resolves merge, rebase, cherry-pick and stash conflicts by intent rather than by line: shows the merge base, reads both sides' commits to state what each change meant to do, writes a resolution that keeps both intents, regenerates lockfiles instead of hand-merging them, hunts semantic conflicts, re-runs build and tests and logs every decision. |
| `/orchestrate` | Designs and runs multi-agent pipelines with EAG subagents: sequential planner-implementer-reviewer chains, parallel fan-out of independent shards with a merge, and adversarial review loops. |
| `/perf-audit` | Audits and fixes performance end to end: sets a target metric and budget, measures a reproducible baseline (Lighthouse, field Core Web Vitals, load tests, benchmarks), profiles to find the dominant bottleneck, fixes one cause at a time and proves each win with before-and-after numbers and a regression guard. |
| `/post-deploy-canary` | Watches a fresh deploy for a fixed window: records a pre-deploy baseline, then polls key pages and endpoints for status codes, error rates, latency, console errors and web vitals, compares each cycle with the baseline using explicit thresholds, gathers evidence such as screenshots and failing requests, and recommends continue or roll back without acting alone. |
| `/postmortem` | Writes a blameless postmortem from an incident: gathers evidence (alerts, logs, deploys, chat), builds a UTC timeline, quantifies impact, separates trigger, root cause and contributing factors, records what went well and where the team got lucky, and turns findings into owned, dated action items. |
| `/pr-ready` | Prepares a branch for a pull request: runs full verification, self-reviews the diff, cleans up commits without force-pushing shared branches, writes the PR title and body (summary, why, changes, testing evidence, risk and rollback, screenshots for UI), adds a changelog entry, and opens the PR with gh only when asked. |
| `/recency-research` | Researches what practitioners and official sources said about a topic in a recent window (30 days by default): searches forums, issue trackers, social posts, video, news and release notes by date, merges duplicates, weights items by engagement and credibility, and writes a dated, cited brief that separates confirmed facts from reports and speculation. |
| `/refactor-clean` | Removes dead code, unused dependencies and duplication in tool-backed, test-guarded batches. |
| `/regression-bisect` | Finds the commit that introduced a regression: writes a deterministic repro script that exits 0 when good and 1 when bad, proves it on a known-good and a known-bad commit, runs git bisect in a separate worktree, skips commits that cannot be tested, then confirms the culprit by reverting it on HEAD and reports the diff with evidence. |
| `/release-management` | Cuts a software release: confirms the commit is green, picks the semantic version from the actual changes, updates the changelog and version files, dry-runs the package, writes release notes, and tags, pushes and publishes only after explicit confirmation, with a rollout and rollback plan. |
| `/research-synthesis` | Answers a research question with real, checked sources: frames the question, searches broadly including for disconfirming evidence, grades credibility, traces claims to primary sources, maps agreement and conflict, and writes a cited report with explicit confidence and open questions. |
| `/review-feedback-response` | Works through code review feedback on a pull request or change: collects every thread, checks each suggestion against the actual code, asks about unclear items before changing anything, pushes back with technical reasons where a suggestion is wrong, implements accepted items one at a time with tests after each, and drafts a reply per thread. |
| `/root-cause` | Debugs systematically instead of guessing: reproduces the failure, minimizes it, ranks falsifiable hypotheses, bisects regressions with git bisect run, instruments to confirm, fixes with a regression test and explains the cause with five whys, keeping a debugging log. |
| `/security-scan` | Runs a layered security scan of a repository or diff: secrets (eag shield, gitleaks), dependency CVEs (npm, pnpm, pip-audit, govulncheck, cargo audit, osv-scanner), static analysis (semgrep, bandit, eslint security rules), config review (Docker, IaC, CORS, headers) and prompt-injection surfaces in LLM features. |
| `/session-resume` | Loads the latest (or a chosen) EAG session summary, re-validates its claims against the current repository (commits, working tree, branch, gates since the summary was written), and produces a short "where we are, what changed, next 3 steps" brief before any work starts. |
| `/session-save` | Writes a rich, resumable session summary (goal, state of work, files touched, decisions and rationale, failed approaches, open questions, exact next steps, commands to re-run) and saves it to the EAG session store so a later conversation or teammate can continue without rediscovery. |
| `/skill-create` | Creates a new Antigravity skill from patterns that repeat in a project: mines git history (recurring commit types, frequently co-changed files), existing conventions and docs, drafts a SKILL.md to the EAG authoring standard in the workspace or global skills directory, validates its frontmatter, and tests it with a fresh agent. |
| `/skill-finder` | Finds the right EAG skill for a goal ("which skill should I use?"): reads the eag-* indexes, shortlists 1-3 with reasons and an order, offers to run the best. |
| `/slice-into-tickets` | Breaks a spec, PRD, design doc or conversation into thin vertical tickets, each end-to-end, demoable and sized for one agent session, with acceptance criteria, a verification command, a size estimate and explicit blocked-by links that form a checked dependency graph, then writes them as local files or, after confirmation, to the issue tracker. |
| `/socratic-tutor` | Teaches a concept or skill in the user's own workspace instead of doing the work: gauges the current level, explains with examples from the user's code, has the user predict outcomes and write the next step, gives graded hints instead of answers, and checks understanding with a transfer exercise. |
| `/tdd` | Drives red-green-refactor: writes a failing test from the requirement, proves it fails for the right reason, adds the minimal code to pass, refactors under green, then checks the new branches are covered. |
| `/terse-mode` | Switches the session into compressed replies that drop greetings, recaps, hedges and filler while keeping code, paths, commands, numbers and error text exact. |
| `/test-coverage` | Measures test coverage, then finds the untested code that matters most (critical paths, error handling, recent churn) instead of chasing a percentage, and writes the missing tests in risk order. |
| `/test-suite-audit` | Audits an existing test suite for tests that cost more than they protect: assertions on mocks instead of behaviour, assertion-free tests, duplicates, tests that read source text, test-only production exports, oversized snapshots and quietly skipped or loosened tests. |
| `/threat-modeling` | Runs a threat model for a feature or system change: scope, data-flow diagram with trust boundaries, STRIDE per element, abuse cases, risk rating, mitigations mapped to owners, and tracked follow-ups. |
| `/throwaway-prototype` | Builds a deliberately disposable prototype to answer one named question, such as whether a state model holds up, which of three layouts feels right, or whether an API behaves as documented. |
| `/ui-polish` | Visually QAs and polishes a UI in a real browser: screenshots across breakpoints, themes and states, then checks spacing, alignment, typography, colour, empty, loading and error states, long content, focus and hover, and motion with reduced-motion, fixes issues through design tokens and proves them with before-and-after screenshots. |
| `/update-docs` | Syncs documentation with code: detects drift from the diff (changed public APIs, CLI flags, env vars, scripts, config keys), updates README, CHANGELOG, API docs, CODEMAP and ADRs, verifies that code samples still run, and delegates large sweeps to the doc-updater subagent. |
| `/verify` | Runs the project's verification gates and prints a VERIFICATION REPORT with PASS, FAIL or SKIP per gate. |
| `/video-render` | Produces a rendered video from a brief: chooses Remotion or ffmpeg, builds the composition, previews key frames, renders a master, verifies duration, resolution, frame rate and loudness with ffprobe and ebur128, and exports platform variants such as 16:9, 9:16 and 1:1. |
| `/write-spec` | Writes a technical spec or design doc for a change: problem, goals and non-goals, current state grounded in the code, a proposed design with interfaces and data model, at least two real alternatives, risks, rollout and rollback, test plan and open review questions, saved as a reviewable artifact. |
| `/yagni-minimalism` | Switches the session into minimal-solution mode until the user turns it off: before each change it tries deleting, reusing, configuring and the standard library before new code, adds no dependency, abstraction, flag or extension point nobody asked for, and re-reads each diff to strip speculative generality, never at the cost of correctness or security. |

## Knowledge skills

Run any of them as a slash command, or let the agent find them through the index named in each heading.

### AI, agents and machine learning (`eag-ai-ml`)

| Skill | What it covers |
| :--- | :--- |
| `agent-design-patterns` | Designs AI agents that behave reliably: choosing between a workflow and an agent, tool design (names, schemas, errors, idempotency), loop patterns such as ReAct, plan-and-execute, router, orchestrator-workers and evaluator-optimizer, memory tiers, human approval gates, budgets and stop conditions, and a failure-mode catalog. |
| `agent-evals` | Evaluates LLM features and agents: golden datasets, programmatic graders, rubric and LLM-as-judge scoring with human calibration, pass@k and pass^k, trajectory evals for tool use, red-team sets, cost and latency tracking, and regression gates in CI, with a minimal Python harness. |
| `antigravity-customization` | Writes Antigravity skills, rules, workflows, subagents, hooks, MCP config and plugins that load correctly and fit the context budget. |
| `antigravity-sdk-orchestrator` | Builds and orchestrates agents in code with the Google Antigravity Python SDK (google-antigravity): Agent and LocalAgentConfig, streaming, custom tools, MCP servers, subagent hierarchies, safety policies and sandboxing, hooks, budgets, retries, compaction, persistence and structured output. |
| `computer-vision` | Builds computer vision systems: framing classification, detection and segmentation tasks, testing Gemini zero-shot before training, dataset collection and labeling guidelines, leakage-safe splits, transfer learning and augmentation, metrics such as mAP, IoU and per-class recall, export to ONNX or LiteRT, and cloud or edge deployment with monitoring. |
| `context-compaction` | Keeps long sessions sharp: when and how to compact, what to keep, handoff notes and session save and resume. |
| `exploratory-data-analysis` | Runs exploratory data analysis on a new dataset: framing questions, profiling schema and types, missing values, duplicates, distributions, outliers, relationships and correlations, time patterns and leakage signals, with pandas, Polars, DuckDB or BigQuery, then reports findings with clear charts and caveats. |
| `gemini-api` | Builds with the Gemini API and Gen AI SDK: model choice, structured output, function calling, caching, files, streaming and cost. |
| `gemma-local-models` | Runs open models such as Gemma locally or on-premises with Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio, MLX or Transformers: sizing model and GGUF quantization to the hardware, memory math, setting context length, OpenAI-compatible local endpoints, structured output, evaluating against a hosted model, licensing, and securing the local server. |
| `google-adk` | Builds agents with Google's Agent Development Kit (google-adk): LLM agents with function tools, coordinator and workflow multi-agent designs, sessions, state and memory, callbacks for guardrails, evaluation with adk eval, and deployment to Cloud Run or Agent Runtime (formerly Vertex AI Agent Engine). |
| `jupyter-notebooks` | Keeps Jupyter notebooks reproducible and reviewable: structure, pinned kernels, restart-and-run-all checks, clean git diffs with nbstripout, Jupytext or nbdime, parameterized runs with papermill, CI execution with nbmake, Colab Enterprise and Vertex AI Workbench, safe agent edits of .ipynb files, and refactoring notebook code into modules and pipelines. |
| `llm-cost-routing` | Cuts LLM spend without losing quality: cost per successful task, routing by difficulty across Gemini tiers, cascades with verifiable confidence checks, thinking-level tuning, implicit and explicit caching, Batch API, token budgets, prompt compression and response caching, plus picking agent models in Antigravity (model: flash, pro or inherit). |
| `llm-fine-tuning` | Decides when to fine-tune an LLM instead of prompting or RAG, then does it: baseline evals, dataset design and cleaning, supervised tuning of Gemini on Vertex AI, LoRA and QLoRA on open models such as Gemma with PEFT and TRL, starting hyperparameters, overfitting checks, evaluation against the prompted baseline, and serving adapters. |
| `llm-observability` | Instruments LLM and agent applications: OpenTelemetry GenAI spans for model, tool and agent steps, token, cost and latency metrics, prompt and model version tags, PII-safe capture of prompts and outputs, Cloud Trace or LLM-focused backends, dashboards and alerts, and user feedback linked to traces for evals. |
| `mcp-server-development` | Builds and debugs MCP servers and clients: tool design, schemas, transports, auth, testing and safe defaults. |
| `ml-evaluation` | Evaluates predictive ML models rigorously: metrics matched to the decision for classification, regression and ranking, split design with group and time splits, leakage hunting, threshold selection, probability calibration, bootstrap confidence intervals and paired significance tests, slice-based error analysis, and a reproducible evaluation report. |
| `ml-experiment-tracking` | Sets up experiment tracking for ML and LLM work with MLflow, Vertex AI Experiments or Weights & Biases: a run contract (params, step metrics, artifacts, git SHA, data and environment versions), a logging helper, model registry versions and aliases, comparing runs, and reproducing a past result. |
| `model-serving` | Serves ML models and open LLMs in production: deciding whether to self-host, latency SLOs (TTFT, inter-token latency, p95), memory and KV-cache sizing, dynamic and continuous batching, quantization, vLLM and other inference servers, GPUs on GKE, Cloud Run or Vertex AI, autoscaling signals, load tests and canary rollouts. |
| `multimodal-understanding` | Builds features that understand images, video, audio and PDFs with Gemini: inline data versus Files API or URLs, media resolution and token cost, prompting for grounded visual answers, bounding boxes, timestamps in video and audio, documents and charts, long-media strategies, and evaluating multimodal output. |
| `prompt-engineering` | Writes and debugs prompts and system instructions for Gemini: structure, examples, output schemas and eval-driven iteration. |
| `pytorch-training` | Builds and debugs PyTorch training code: Dataset and DataLoader setup, a correct train and eval loop, mixed precision with autocast, gradient clipping, resumable checkpoints, torch.compile, multi-GPU with torchrun and DDP, determinism, and a triage procedure for NaN or exploding losses. |
| `rag-pipelines` | Builds retrieval-augmented generation pipelines: choosing between RAG, long context and context caching, chunking, Gemini embeddings, hybrid keyword plus vector search, reranking, pgvector, AlloyDB and Vertex AI Vector Search, citation grounding, freshness, and retrieval and faithfulness evals. |
| `recommender-systems` | Designs recommender systems: objective and guardrails, impression logging, popularity and co-visitation baselines, candidate generation with matrix factorization, two-tower retrieval and content embeddings, ranking with gradient boosting, re-ranking for diversity and business rules, cold start, offline metrics such as recall@k and NDCG, and A/B testing. |
| `responsible-ai` | Applies responsible AI practice to ML and generative AI features: use-case and harm review, fairness evaluation across groups, layered safety controls for Gemini apps, human oversight, model cards and AI disclosure, provenance with SynthID, policy and regulatory checklists, and incident response. |
| `speech-ai` | Builds speech features: transcription with Cloud Speech-to-Text or Gemini audio understanding, speaker diarization, streaming recognition, text-to-speech with Cloud Text-to-Speech or Gemini speech generation, realtime voice agents and latency budgets, audio formats, WER and diarization evaluation, and recording and voice consent. |
| `structured-extraction` | Extracts structured data from text, PDFs, images and long documents with Gemini: a labeled golden set, schemas with null and evidence fields, schema-constrained output, semantic validation with one repair retry, chunking and merging for long inputs, batch runs, and field-level precision and recall evaluation. |

| `firestore-data-modeling` | Designs Cloud Firestore data models: documents versus subcollections, denormalization and fan-out, query and composite index planning, hotspot and write-rate limits, counters, pagination, how security rules constrain query shape, and read/write cost control. |
| `mongodb` | Models and operates MongoDB: embed-versus-reference decisions, schema design patterns, compound indexes with the ESR rule, explain plans, aggregation pipelines, multi-document transactions, schema validation, sharding keys, and Atlas operations (Performance Advisor, backups, network and user access). |
| `mysql-mariadb` | Designs and tunes MySQL and MariaDB on InnoDB: clustered primary keys, secondary and covering indexes, EXPLAIN ANALYZE, slow-log and performance_schema triage, locking and deadlocks, replication lag, and online schema changes (INSTANT/INPLACE DDL, gh-ost, pt-online-schema-change). |
| `orm-patterns` | Uses ORMs and query builders well: Prisma, Drizzle, SQLAlchemy 2.0 and TypeORM. |
| `postgres-patterns` | Applies PostgreSQL features in depth: JSONB modelling and GIN indexes, CTEs and recursive queries, window functions, upserts and SKIP LOCKED queues, declarative partitioning, row-level security for multi-tenant data, extensions, and autovacuum, bloat and wraparound health. |
| `pyspark` | Writes and tunes PySpark jobs on Dataproc, Serverless for Apache Spark or any Spark cluster: DataFrame API idioms, lazy evaluation, partitioning and shuffles, join strategies and skew handling with AQE and salting, Python UDF costs versus built-ins and pandas UDFs, caching, file layout, the BigQuery connector, and pytest testing. |
| `sql-optimization` | Diagnoses and fixes slow SQL across PostgreSQL and MySQL: finding the expensive statements, reading execution plans, index design, sargability and other query anti-patterns, statistics and misestimates, keyset pagination, and batched writes and bulk loads. |
| `stream-processing` | Designs streaming pipelines on Dataflow with Apache Beam, on Apache Flink, or with Kafka Streams: event time versus processing time, windows, watermarks, triggers and allowed lateness, keyed state and timers, exactly-once semantics end to end, dead-letter handling, pipeline updates and drains, and testing. |
| `vector-databases` | Chooses, configures and evaluates vector stores: pgvector on Cloud SQL or AlloyDB, AlloyDB ScaNN indexes, Vertex AI Vector Search, BigQuery and Firestore vector search. |

### Testing and code quality (`eag-testing-quality`)

| Skill | What it covers |
| :--- | :--- |
| `api-testing` | Builds API test suites that catch real bugs: in-process HTTP tests (supertest, httpx with FastAPI, Go httptest, Spring MockMvc), black-box suites against deployed environments (Postman/Newman, Bruno, Hurl, .http files), auth and object-level authorization matrices, OpenAPI response validation and Schemathesis fuzzing. |
| `concurrency-bugs` | Debugs concurrency defects: data races, check-then-act and lost updates, deadlocks, livelocks, ordering and visibility bugs, async pitfalls (missing await, blocked event loops) and duplicate processing across services. |
| `contract-testing` | Sets up contract testing between services: consumer-driven contracts with Pact (consumer tests, provider verification, broker, can-i-deploy), provider states and loose matchers, plus schema-diff gates in CI for OpenAPI (oasdiff), protobuf (buf breaking), GraphQL (GraphQL Inspector) and event schemas, and API versioning rules. |
| `flaky-test-triage` | Diagnoses and fixes non-deterministic tests: measures the flake rate with repeated runs, classifies the cause (async timing, order pollution, shared state, network, clock, randomness, resources), replaces sleeps with condition polling, bisects test order to find the polluter, seeds randomness and freezes clocks. |
| `legacy-modernization` | Modernizes legacy systems incrementally: mapping hidden consumers, characterization tests, seams and branch by abstraction, the strangler fig pattern behind a routing facade, anti-corruption layers, shadow traffic and parallel runs, data migration with CDC and reconciliation, and the rewrite-versus-refactor decision. |
| `linting-formatting` | Sets up and enforces linters and formatters across languages: Prettier, Biome and ESLint, Ruff, gofmt and golangci-lint, rustfmt and Clippy, dotnet format, clang-format, shellcheck and PSScriptAnalyzer, with pinned versions, pre-commit hooks, CI check mode, autofix, and adopting them in legacy repos without wrecking git blame. |
| `memory-leaks` | Finds and fixes memory leaks: telling leaks from caches and fragmentation, three-snapshot heap diffs, retainer paths and dominator trees, with tools per runtime (DevTools heap snapshots for Node.js and browsers, tracemalloc and memray for Python, pprof and goleak for Go, jcmd and Eclipse MAT for the JVM, dotnet-gcdump, ASan and Valgrind). |
| `mutation-testing` | Measures whether tests actually catch bugs by injecting small faults with Stryker, mutmut, PIT or cargo-mutants, scoped to changed code first, then triages surviving mutants into equivalent, missing assertion or untested branch and writes targeted tests to kill the ones that matter. |
| `profiling` | Profiles CPU, wall-clock and allocation hot spots across runtimes: pprof for Go, py-spy and cProfile for Python, --cpu-prof and DevTools for Node.js, async-profiler and JFR for the JVM, perf and cargo flamegraph for native and Rust, dotnet-trace, Cloud Profiler in production, and how to read flame graphs and prove a fix with benchmarks. |
| `property-based-testing` | Writes property-based tests that state invariants instead of examples, with Hypothesis, fast-check, jqwik, proptest and rapid: round trips, idempotence, oracles, metamorphic and stateful model tests, generators that reach edge cases, shrinking to minimal counterexamples, CI seeds and run budgets. |
| `safe-refactor` | Changes code structure without changing behaviour: characterization and approval tests, a refactoring catalogue with safety ratings, strangler fig, parallel change, branch by abstraction, feature flags, micro-commits, codemods (jscodeshift, ts-morph, ast-grep, LibCST, gofmt -r, gopls) and ways to prove zero behaviour change. |
| `static-analysis` | Runs and tunes static analysis for bugs and security: Semgrep (registry rulesets, custom rules with tests, diff-aware scans), CodeQL, SonarQube quality gates and language-native analysers such as Bandit, gosec, staticcheck and clang-tidy, plus SARIF output, triage of true and false positives, suppressions with reasons and new-code-only CI gates. |
| `tdd-testing` | Test-driven development: failing test first, smallest change to pass, refactor, and test design across unit to e2e. |
| `tech-debt` | Manages technical debt as a ranked, owned register: finding debt from churn and complexity hotspots, TODOs, incidents and developer surveys, scoring interest against principal, choosing a paydown strategy (boy scout, pay before feature work, capacity allocation, dedicated projects), and explaining its cost to product and leadership. |
| `test-data-management` | Manages test data so suites are fast, isolated and safe: factories (factory_boy, FactoryBot, fishery), minimal fixtures, idempotent seeds, per-test isolation with transactions, truncation, per-worker or template databases and Testcontainers, deterministic fakes and clocks, and masked or synthetic data. |
| `visual-regression` | Sets up visual regression testing that catches real UI changes without flaking: Playwright toHaveScreenshot baselines, thresholds and masks, deterministic rendering (fonts, animations, clock, network), per-platform baselines in Docker or CI, Storybook component snapshots with Chromatic or similar services, and a baseline review workflow. |

| :--- | :--- |

| `cloud-security-posture` | Finds and fixes cloud misconfigurations: public exposure, over-broad IAM, service-account keys, missing org policies and logging gaps, using Security Command Center, Cloud Asset Inventory, IAM Recommender, Prowler and IaC scanners, with fixes landed through Terraform. |

| `cryptography` | Applied cryptography for application engineers: choosing primitives (AEAD, hashes, MACs, signatures, key exchange), password hashing parameters, secure randomness, envelope encryption and key management with Cloud KMS and Tink, TLS configuration, constant-time comparison, post-quantum planning and the common mistakes reviewers catch. |
| `defense-in-depth-validation` | Hardens code after a bad-data bug is root-caused by adding a check at every layer the data crosses: schema parsing at the entry point, invariants in domain types, context guards before destructive operations, database constraints and diagnostic logging at the failure point, each with its own test. |
| `gdpr-privacy` | Privacy engineering for GDPR and CCPA/CPRA basics: data mapping and records of processing, lawful basis and consent capture, data subject requests (access, deletion, portability), retention and deletion pipelines, pseudonymization, DPIAs and breach timelines. |
| `hipaa-compliance` | HIPAA for engineers: identifying PHI, covered entities versus business associates, BAAs with every vendor in the PHI path, Security Rule technical safeguards (access control, audit logs, integrity, authentication, transmission security), de-identification, breach notification timelines and keeping PHI out of logs and tools. |
| `llm-app-security` | Secures applications and agents built on LLMs: direct and indirect prompt injection, data exfiltration through tools and rendered output, excessive agency, RAG access control, system prompt leakage, output handling, cost abuse, and red-team testing mapped to the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications. |
| `pci-dss` | PCI DSS scope reduction for engineers: what counts as account data, keeping card data off your systems with hosted fields and tokenization, network segmentation, choosing the likely SAQ type, payment-page script controls, PAN detection in logs, and evidence for assessors. |
| `sandbox-isolation` | Sets up least-privilege execution for agents: the Antigravity terminal sandbox and agy --sandbox, permission rules, per-agent commandExecutionPolicy, devcontainers, Docker with dropped capabilities, read-only filesystem and no network, gVisor, egress allowlists, and separate cloud projects and credentials. |
| `secrets-management` | Stores, injects and rotates secrets: Google Secret Manager with per-secret IAM, Vault and dynamic credentials, runtime injection on Cloud Run, GKE and VMs, keyless CI with Workload Identity Federation, rotation without downtime, BuildKit build secrets, and stopping leaks through env vars, logs, images and Git. |
| `security-audit` | Audits code and config for OWASP Top 10, secrets, authz gaps, injection and dependency risk, with ranked fixes. |
| `soc2-compliance` | Guides SOC 2 readiness for engineering teams: choosing Trust Services Criteria, scoping the system, gap assessment, policies, implementing and automating controls (access reviews, change management, vulnerability and incident management), evidence collection, and working with the auditor through Type I and Type II. |
| `supply-chain-security` | Secures the software supply chain: lockfiles and hash pinning, dependency review and admission rules, SBOM generation and scanning, SLSA build provenance, Sigstore signing and verification, CI workflow hardening and dependency-confusion defenses. |
| `web-pentest-authorized` | Methodology for authorized web application penetration testing: written scope and rules of engagement, test environment setup, OWASP WSTG coverage, evidence handling, severity rating and a reproducible report with retest. |

| `podcast-production` | Produces podcasts end to end: show format and run-of-show, recording setup and gain staging, remote double-ender recording, editing, a voice processing chain, two-pass loudness normalization with ffmpeg, MP3 export and ID3 tags, transcripts, show notes with chapters, artwork specs, and RSS distribution to Apple Podcasts, Spotify and YouTube. |
| `presentation-slides` | Builds presentation decks that land: audience and goal framing, storyline written as action titles before any slide exists, slide layout and type rules, data slides with one message per chart, speaker notes, accessible slides, and tooling from Google Slides and PowerPoint to Marp, Slidev, reveal.js and python-pptx. |
| `remotion-motion-graphics` | Builds programmatic videos with Remotion (React): compositions, useCurrentFrame, interpolate and spring animation, Sequence and Series timing, audio sync, fonts and assets via staticFile, captions, data-driven props, and local or cloud rendering with performance tuning. |
| `svg-graphics` | Authors and ships SVG: hand-written icons on a viewBox grid with currentColor, path command basics, SVGO optimization that keeps viewBox and IDs, inline versus img versus sprite delivery with symbol and use, CSS animation with reduced-motion support, accessible titles and roles, and sanitizing untrusted SVG uploads. |
| `ui-ux-design` | Designs usable interfaces from problem to handoff: framing, user flows with error paths, low-fidelity wireframes, complete component states, responsive layouts, heuristic evaluation with severity ratings, structured design critique, Figma handoff with auto layout, variables and annotations, and design QA against the built UI in a browser. |
| `ux-research` | Plans and runs UX research: choosing methods by question, recruiting with screeners and consent, interview guides about past behaviour, moderated usability tests with task success, SEQ and SUS, unbiased surveys with sample sizes, and synthesis from transcripts into affinity clusters, evidence-backed insights, personas and jobs to be done. |
| `video-production-pipeline` | Runs end-to-end video production from brief to delivered files: script, storyboard, asset list, TTS voice-over with Google Cloud Text-to-Speech or Gemini TTS, editing in Remotion or ffmpeg, captions, loudness mastering, platform exports for YouTube, Shorts, Reels and TikTok, and a QA checklist. |
| `visual-identity` | Creates a visual identity system: brief and moodboards, logo concept exploration and stress tests (favicon size, one colour, reversed), colour systems with tonal scales and contrast-checked pairs, typography with licensing checks, brand guidelines, design tokens and asset packages, and trademark and originality checks. |
| `youtube-channel` | Grows and runs a YouTube channel: audience and content pillars, packaging ideas before scripting, titles and thumbnails, hooks and retention-focused scripts and edits, chapters, captions and end screens, Shorts, reading YouTube Studio analytics (CTR, average view duration, retention graphs, traffic sources), and metadata automation with the YouTube APIs. |

### Developer workflow and tooling (`eag-dev-tooling`)

| Skill | What it covers |
| :--- | :--- |
| `browser-extensions` | Builds Manifest V3 browser extensions for Chrome, Edge and Firefox: minimal permissions, service worker lifecycle, content scripts and isolated worlds, runtime messaging, storage, declarativeNetRequest, cross-browser builds with WXT or web-ext, automated tests with Playwright, and store review and privacy requirements. |
| `cli-development` | Builds command-line tools people and scripts can rely on: argument parsing in Node, Python, Go and Rust, help text, stdout versus stderr, JSON output, exit codes, config and env precedence, TTY and NO_COLOR handling, safe destructive commands, signal handling, testing, and packaging for npm, PyPI, Go and Cargo. |
| `dev-environments` | Builds reproducible developer environments: pinned toolchains with mise, asdf or version files, Dev Containers and the devcontainer CLI, Nix dev shells, local services with Docker Compose, env templates, dotfiles, and idempotent bootstrap scripts for bash and PowerShell. |
| `diagrams-as-code` | Produces diagrams as editable text with Mermaid, D2 or Excalidraw JSON: picks the diagram type for the question (flow, sequence, ER, state, C4 context or container), derives nodes and edges from the real repository (manifests, imports, routes, schemas) instead of guessing, renders to SVG or PNG, checks the image, and commits source beside output. |
| `documentation-writing` | Writes READMEs, guides, API references, ADRs and changelogs that are task-first, accurate and tested. |
| `docx-documents` | Creates and edits Word .docx files with python-docx and pandoc: template styles instead of direct formatting, headings, tables, images, headers and footers, page numbers and tables of contents, plus tracked changes and comments so edits stay reviewable. |
| `file-backed-planning` | Keeps an agent's working memory for long, multi-step tasks in three small project files: a plan with phases and status, a findings log with sources, and a progress log that records every error and attempted fix. |
| `fresh-docs-lookup` | Grounds code against third-party libraries, SDKs and CLIs in the version the project actually uses: reads the lockfile, checks the installed package's own types and docs, fetches versioned official docs, changelogs or a docs MCP server, verifies signatures by compiling or calling them, and cites the source. |
| `git-workflow` | Branches, commits, rebases, conflict resolution, PR hygiene and recovery from git mistakes without losing work. |
| `google-apps-script` | Automates Google Workspace with Apps Script: local development with clasp, the appsscript.json manifest and least-privilege OAuth scopes, batched Sheets reads and writes, simple versus installable triggers, quotas, time limits and checkpointed long jobs, LockService, script properties, custom functions, and web app or add-on deployment. |
| `ide-extensions` | Builds extensions for VS Code-compatible editors, including the Antigravity IDE: scaffolding, package.json contributions, lazy activation events, commands, settings, SecretStorage, webviews with CSP, language servers, integration tests with @vscode/test-cli, VSIX packaging, and publishing to the VS Code Marketplace and Open VSX. |
| `interactive-cli-driving` | Operates programs that need a live terminal (REPLs, debuggers such as pdb, gdb and lldb, database shells, interactive installers and full-screen TUIs) by running them in a named, detached tmux session or under pexpect, sending keys, capturing the screen and polling for prompts instead of sleeping. |
| `open-source-maintenance` | Sets up and runs an open-source project: license choice and dependency license checks, community health files, issue forms and PR templates, CONTRIBUTING, CODEOWNERS and DCO/CLA flow, governance and maintainer roles, SECURITY.md with private vulnerability reporting, and sustainable triage habits. |
| `pdf-toolkit` | Works with PDFs end to end using open tools: inspects with pdfinfo and qpdf, extracts text and tables with pdftotext and pdfplumber, OCRs scans with ocrmypdf, merges, splits, rotates and stamps with qpdf or pypdf, reads and fills form fields, generates PDFs from HTML or Markdown, redacts properly, and renders pages to images to verify every result. |
| `regex-text-processing` | Writes correct, safe regular expressions and text pipelines: engine differences (PCRE2, JavaScript, Python, RE2/Go/Rust, POSIX), ReDoS avoidance, ripgrep, sed, awk, jq, yq, Miller and PowerShell equivalents, test-first patterns, preview-then-replace edits, and streaming large files. |
| `sdk-generation` | Produces client SDKs from API contracts: OpenAPI and protobuf linting, generator choice (openapi-typescript, OpenAPI Generator, oapi-codegen, Kiota, buf), handwritten ergonomic wrappers for auth, retries, pagination and typed errors, regeneration checks and breaking-change detection in CI, and SDK versioning and publishing. |
| `spreadsheet-modeling` | Builds robust spreadsheet models and dashboards in Excel and Google Sheets: inputs-calcs-outputs layout, named inputs with data validation, consistent formulas with XLOOKUP, SUMIFS, LET and FILTER, check cells, scenarios and sensitivity tables, pivot tables, dashboards, and generating workbooks from code. |
| `task-runners` | Designs a project's command surface with Make, just, npm/pnpm scripts, Taskfile or mise tasks: standard task names, one entry point shared by developers and CI, argument passing, dependencies, incremental builds, and Windows-compatible commands. |

| `ai-search-visibility` | Improves how often a site is cited by AI answer engines and AI overviews without manipulation: audits AI crawler access in robots.txt, CDN rules and server rendering, adds llms.txt and matching JSON-LD, restructures pages into quotable answers with clear entities and sources, builds third-party evidence, and measures citations over a fixed query set. |

| `okrs` | Writes, reviews and scores OKRs: qualitative objectives, outcome key results with baselines and targets, committed versus aspirational goals, health metrics, cascading and cross-team alignment, weekly check-ins, end-of-cycle scoring and guarding against sandbagging and task-list key results. |

| `people-operations` | Runs everyday people operations for small and growing teams: onboarding plans (30/60/90), 1:1s, feedback with the SBI model, goals, performance review cycles with calibration and bias checks, underperformance, offboarding, and remote or hybrid norms. |
| `pitch-deck` | Builds and critiques fundraising pitch decks: the one-line ask, a headline narrative, slide order from pre-seed to Series A, bottom-up market sizing, traction with defined metrics, honest competition, use of funds, design for sent and presented versions, investor red-teaming and data-room readiness. |
| `policy-drafting` | Drafts and maintains privacy policies, terms of service, cookie notices and internal policies (acceptable use, security, remote work, generative AI use, expenses) from an inventory of actual practice, using clause checklists, plain-language rules and versioning. |
| `pricing-strategy` | Designs pricing and packaging for SaaS, open-core, API and LLM-powered products: value metric selection, good/better/best tiers, freemium vs free trial, usage-based billing with model-cost pass-through, ethical price testing, pricing page anatomy, enterprise packaging and grandfathering. |
| `product-analytics` | Designs product analytics: question-driven tracking plans, event naming taxonomy, identity and consent, North Star and input metrics, activation, funnels, retention cohorts, engagement ratios, dashboards and data QA in GA4 and BigQuery, Amplitude, Mixpanel or PostHog. |
| `product-discovery` | Runs product discovery to decide what is worth building: outcome framing, opportunity mapping, customer interviews about past behaviour, synthesis with verbatim evidence, assumption mapping across value, usability, feasibility and viability, and cheap tests such as fake doors, concierge and prototype sessions. |
| `product-requirements` | Writes and reviews product requirements documents (PRDs): problem statement, target users and evidence, goals and success metrics with guardrails, scope and non-goals, numbered requirements with acceptance criteria, risks, rollout and the review process. |
| `roadmap-prioritization` | Builds and communicates product roadmaps and ranks backlogs: one intake list, capacity allocation, RICE, ICE, cost of delay and WSJF scoring in a sheet, logged overrides, now-next-later and outcome-based roadmaps, stakeholder alignment and saying no. |
| `sales-outreach` | Plans and drafts outbound sales outreach: ideal customer profile and personas, trigger-based account lists, tiered research and personalization, multi-touch sequences, cold email structure, deliverability, CAN-SPAM, GDPR, PECR and CASL basics, reply handling and follow-ups. |
| `seo-audit` | Runs a technical SEO audit of a site, docs portal or landing page: crawlability (robots.txt, sitemaps, canonicals), indexation, SSR vs CSR rendering, Core Web Vitals, JSON-LD structured data, meta, Open Graph and Twitter cards, hreflang, internal links and content gaps, then returns a prioritized report. |
| `social-media` | Plans and runs organic social media: platform choice by audience, content pillars, calendars, native formats (short video, carousels, threads, live), approval workflow, community replies and escalation, disclosure rules, crisis handling and analytics. |
| `unit-economics` | Calculates unit economics: gross margin with full cost of revenue, blended, paid and fully loaded CAC, churn, LTV, CAC payback, contribution margin by segment, NRR and GRR, and AI cost per user from token and infrastructure usage at median and heavy-user percentiles. |

### Writing, research and education (`eag-writing-research`)

| Skill | What it covers |
| :--- | :--- |
| `conference-talks` | Prepares conference and meetup talks: choosing a talk-worthy idea, CFP abstracts reviewers accept, a narrative with one takeaway, slides readable from the back row, demos that cannot fail (recorded fallback, offline data, scripted state), timing, rehearsal and Q&A. |
| `curriculum-design` | Designs courses, workshops and training with backward design: audience analysis, measurable learning objectives using Bloom's verbs, assessments aligned to each objective, hands-on exercises with checkpoints and solutions, timed pacing plans, and pilot-and-revise loops. |
| `data-storytelling` | Turns analysis into decisions: frames the question and audience, picks the chart that matches the comparison, strips clutter, annotates the takeaway on the chart, builds a narrative arc and writes executive summaries that lead with the answer. |
| `de-slop-prose` | Finds and rewrites the recognizable tells of machine-generated writing: inflated significance, brochure adjectives, reflexive triplets, manufactured "not X but Y" contrasts, stacked hedges, vague attributions, filler transitions, chat residue and echo conclusions. |
| `editing` | Edits and proofreads prose in separate passes: structural edit (purpose, audience, order), line edit (clarity, concision, active voice, plain language), copy edit (style-guide consistency, terminology, numbers) and proofread, returning changes with reasons while keeping the author's voice. |
| `grant-writing` | Writes grant proposals that map to reviewer criteria: funder-fit analysis, a compliance checklist from the call, specific aims, significance and innovation, an approach with risks and alternatives, budgets with justifications, timelines and milestones, and evaluation plans. |
| `internal-comms` | Writes internal communications from real sources: progress-plans-problems updates, weekly status reports, leadership summaries, incident and outage notices, change and reorg announcements, FAQs and team newsletters. |
| `knowledge-management` | Builds team knowledge bases people actually use: content inventory, information architecture by audience and task, Diataxis doc types, docs-as-code with review and link checks, ownership and freshness metadata, decision logs, and pruning stale pages. |
| `literature-review` | Runs academic literature reviews: question framing (PICO and similar), reproducible search strings across databases, PRISMA-style screening against inclusion criteria, structured extraction notes, quality appraisal, thematic synthesis and citation-manager hygiene with Zotero and BibTeX. |
| `newsletters` | Runs newsletters that keep readers: positioning and a reader promise, a cadence the team can sustain, a repeatable issue structure, subject lines and preview text, growth loops, list hygiene and deliverability basics, and metrics beyond opens. |
| `technical-blogging` | Writes technical blog posts engineers finish and trust: a sharp angle, a reader-first structure, runnable code samples, measured proof instead of adjectives, honest trade-offs and distribution that fits the audience. |
| `translation` | Translates and localizes content with quality controls: source preparation, termbases and do-not-translate lists, tone and formality per locale, locale conventions, machine translation with post-editing, placeholder checks, native review loops and MQM-style quality scoring. |

## Rules

| File | Trigger | Scope |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `AGENTS.md` | always_on | every turn |
| `containers.md` | glob | **/Dockerfile, **/Dockerfile.*, **/*.dockerfile, **/docker-compose*.yml, **/compose*.yaml |
| `cpp.md` | glob | **/*.c, **/*.cc, **/*.cpp, **/*.h, **/*.hpp |
| `csharp.md` | glob | **/*.cs |
| `dart-flutter.md` | glob | **/*.dart |
| `elixir.md` | glob | **/*.ex, **/*.exs, **/*.heex |
